messages.content:
The record:
Write the postmortem for the incident below.

Alert: HighErrorRate on io-shop
What the alert said [AL1]: Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}
Alert raised: 2026-11-12T19:19:04Z {alert_raised}
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one. An alert rule fires; a person is paged. Argus first posted about the incident in Slack at 2026-11-12T19:19:28Z {first_told}, and the document says so already: leave that post out, and do not say that no person was told. That nobody was paged is a finding of its own.
The alert rule waits 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding before it fires. The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds {accounted_for} accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes {rule_waits} with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute {rule_evaluated_every}, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds {scraping_allowance} for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
Broken from 2026-11-12T19:13:00Z {began} (the onset). The service was not back to normal by 2026-11-12T19:19:53Z {argus_stopped}, so it was broken for at least 6 minutes 53 seconds {duration} - a lower bound, not a measurement, and every impact figure below is bounded the same way.
Argus held the incident for 27 seconds {held}, until 2026-11-12T19:19:53Z {argus_stopped}. That is not how long the fault lasted, nor how long Argus went on working - leave it out of your answer.
The service's error rate over all its requests, before it began: 0.9% {errors_before}.
The same rate while it was broken: 97.4% {errors_while_broken}, peaking at 100.0% {errors_at_worst}.
Rise above baseline: 96.4% {errors_rise} of traffic failed that otherwise would not have.
The series behind the alert, `sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[1m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[1m]))` - its alert said "Error rate above threshold for 5m {A1}" - which its alert rule evaluates and calls worse rising: 0.9250000000000001% {series_before} before it began, 97.35714285714285% {series_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and 100% {series_at_worst} at its worst. Say what it measures in words, not by its query.
Customer loss: at least 14,635.76 USD {customer_loss} - how far the shop's takings over the incident fell short of the same hours whole weeks earlier, beyond how much those hours vary on their own; a lower bound, counted with the service not seen back to normal.

What Argus did, in order:
  - [T1] 2026-11-12T19:19:25Z {T1.1} Argus: Received HighErrorRate on io-shop
  - [T2] 2026-11-12T19:19:30Z {T2.1} Argus: Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
  - [T3] 2026-11-12T19:19:30Z {T3.1} Argus: Called in the Investigator Agent
  - [T4] 2026-11-12T19:19:38Z {T4.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 19:19:04 {T4.2}
  - [T5] 2026-11-12T19:19:42Z {T5.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 360 {T5.2} minutes of metrics
  - [T6] 2026-11-12T19:19:44Z {T6.1} Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 19:13 {T6.2}
  - [T7] 2026-11-12T19:19:44Z {T7.1} Investigator Agent: Recorded where the 3 {T7.2} replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
  - [T8] 2026-11-12T19:19:45Z {T8.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 1 {T8.2} day 1 {T8.3} minute before Nov 12 19:14 {T8.4}
  - [T9] 2026-11-12T19:19:46Z {T9.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 0 {T9.2} production changes
  - [T10] 2026-11-12T19:19:46Z {T10.1} Investigator Agent: Read the service register - the service calls io-pricing (internal, owned by checkout-platform), io-summary-cache (internal, owned by checkout-platform), io-pay (third-party, owned by IO Payments Ltd)
  - [T11] 2026-11-12T19:19:46Z {T11.1} Investigator Agent: Asked for the service's log lines, the 36 {T11.2} minutes 4 {T11.3} seconds before 19:19:04 {T11.4}
  - [T12] 2026-11-12T19:19:46Z {T12.1} Investigator Agent: Read back 94 {T12.2} log lines
  - [T13] 2026-11-12T19:19:48Z {T13.1} Investigator Agent: Formed 1 {T13.2} candidate cause, best first: C1
  - [T14] 2026-11-12T19:19:48Z {T14.1} Investigator Agent: Read every channel available
  - [T15] 2026-11-12T19:19:48Z {T15.1} Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 0 {T15.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 {T15.3} hour before 19:19:48 {T15.4}
  - [T16] 2026-11-12T19:19:52Z {T16.1} Argus: Moved the incident to MITIGATING to act on a candidate
  - [T17] 2026-11-12T19:19:52Z {T17.1} Argus: Refused to act on C1 - the failure is in a service another company runs, and nothing Argus can do reaches it - ask IO Payments Ltd to restore io-pay, and no code fix is looked for
  - [T18] 2026-11-12T19:19:52Z {T18.1} Argus: Moved the incident to FIXING - no mitigation taken
  - [T19] 2026-11-12T19:19:53Z {T19.1} Argus: Moved the incident to ESCALATED - no code fix looked for

Changes to production it read:
  - Deploys read, none came back; flags read, none came back.

Log lines it read, one per message:
  - [G46bc] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 43 {G46bc.1} occurrences in 29 {G46bc.2} minutes, 18:43–19:11 {G46bc.3}
  - [Gbac1] WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 31 {Gbac1.1} occurrences in 37 {Gbac1.2} minutes, 18:43–19:19 {Gbac1.3}; # was 0.50% {Gbac1.4} to 100.00% {Gbac1.5}, typically 1.50% {Gbac1.6}, highest at 19:14 {Gbac1.7}
  - [Gad41] INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 6 {Gad41.1} occurrences in 29 {Gad41.2} minutes, 18:44–19:12 {Gad41.3}
  - [Gbf7d] ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - PaymentProviderFailed: api.io-pay.example returned 503 {Gbf7d.1} for /v1/shoppers/shopper-#-#-#/card at src/io_shop/payment_provider.py:95 - 14 {Gbf7d.2} occurrences in 7 {Gbf7d.3} minutes, 19:13–19:19 {Gbf7d.4}; /v1/shoppers/shopper-#-#-#/card took 14 {Gbf7d.5} different values

Candidates it considered, in the Investigator's words - name them by their labels, but cite none; what they claim is not what happened unless a row of the record shows it:
  - [C1] From 2026-11-12T19:13:00Z {C1.1} the third-party payment provider io-pay (api.io-pay.example, owned by IO Payments Ltd) began returning 503s {C1.2} on the card lookup. Every account page render calls it, so the error rate went to 100% {C1.3} and latency rose to about 2s {C1.4}. No deploy, flag or rollout change on io-shop, and cpu and memory were flat. [upstream-dependency-failure, confidence 0.93 {C1.5}, never tried: the failure is in a service another company runs, and nothing Argus can do reaches it]

Actions it took:
  - none

Action items the record already holds:
  - AI-1 (mitigate, open): Ask IO Payments Ltd to restore io-pay (api.io-pay.example) and to say why it failed
IO Payments Ltd runs io-pay, so no code fix was looked for: AI-1 asks them to restore it - propose no item of your own for it.

Cite evidence in causal_chain by its label. In a contributing factor's addressed_by, name the record's own action items that answer it, by their number; an item you propose names the factors it answers in its answers, by their labels.

Call submit_postmortem with your answer.

The document, by field:
root_cause: Account page requests in io-shop call the card lookup of io-pay, a payment provider run by IO Payments Ltd. From the onset io-pay answered that lookup with {Gbf7d.1}, and io-shop raised this as PaymentProviderFailed and failed the whole account page request.
cause_in_plain_words: The outside payment company that the shop asks for a shopper's saved card started rejecting those requests, and the shop's account pages failed every time that request failed.
still_at_risk: Account pages could keep failing for as long as io-pay keeps rejecting the card lookup, and could fail the same way the next time io-pay has trouble.
symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
causal_chain 1: Shoppers' account pages failed to load. io-shop's own log reported that the account page error rate was at its worst, and from the onset account page requests failed. (cites Gbac1, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; Gbf7d, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; T6, under "What Argus did, in order")
causal_chain 2: Account page requests failed because the card lookup that io-shop makes to the third-party payment provider io-pay returned {Gbf7d.1}. io-shop raised this as PaymentProviderFailed at src/io_shop/payment_provider.py:95 and failed the request. (cites Gbf7d, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; T10, under "What Argus did, in order")
causal_chain 3: io-pay, which IO Payments Ltd runs, began returning {Gbf7d.1} on the card lookup at the onset. The record does not show why: io-pay's own state was not read, only io-shop's logs of its replies. (cites Gbf7d, under "Log lines it read, one per message"; T10, under "What Argus did, in order")
contributing_factors 1: When io-pay's card lookup failed, io-shop failed the whole account page request. No fallback was seen, such as rendering the page without the card details or using a cached copy.
contributing_factors 1 had_it_been_otherwise: Account pages would have loaded without card details while io-pay was failing, so most shoppers would have seen a page that still worked instead of an error.
contributing_factors 2: The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop was not linked to any on-call incident, so nobody was paged when it fired.
contributing_factors 2 had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been engaged when the alert fired and could have asked IO Payments Ltd to restore io-pay sooner, which would have shortened the outage.
action_items 1: Make the io-shop account page render without card details, instead of failing the request, when io-pay's card lookup returns an error.
action_items 2: Add a test that the account page still renders when io-pay's card lookup returns {Gbf7d.1}.
action_items 3: Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to the on-call paging rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {T5.1} or {duration}, are figures code writes in from the row they name. They are not judged.
  - Action items propose what to do; they make no claim about the record.
  - Whether something went well, went wrong or was lucky is a judgement. Only a fact it states is judged, and whether a went_wrong item is one its field excludes.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
